events.text: Office rebuilt against your reference photos: maple desks, brass saucers, grid windows, checkerboard jute.
Read the finance files - they are already on the new numbers, so the stale stuff is mostly in the older brand, sales and supplier files.
Found the trap: in the match trade a 'veneer matchbox' often means veneer OUTER shell with a cardboard inner tray. Asking every vendor which part is wood.
Most Pune printer websites are blocked (403) - working from search snippets and marking numbers UNVERIFIED.
Biggest catch: our own vendor message asks for pink and black match heads, and colour matches are treated differently in law from safety matches - confirm in writing before ordering
Delivered the Drop 01 law map, a 12-line dashboard checklist, and legal notes for the box printing, website, Instagram, cafe and vendor tasks
Starting the consistency sweep across all the older files.
Verifying real Pune venues via web search — no invented names allowed.
Three design agendas written plus a one-page priority sheet. Run packaging first this weekend, social on Wednesday, leave the website alone until 22 September.
Law map is written - seven stages, from the Sivakasi invoice to the Instagram caption, with what each one costs
Every company website is blocked on this machine (403). I am building the comparison from search snippets and saying so in every row.
Started on seeding list, WhatsApp messages and hand-delivery plan for Drop 01 (300 boxes, Pune only).
Started printer + striker strip research for Drop 01 sleeves.
Started printer + striker strip research for Drop 01 sleeves.
Business model changed: I am now sourcing plain wooden-veneer trays in bulk, not custom printed boxes.
Caught a date clash: the 30-day Instagram plan has you posting SOLD OUT and packing orders in week 4, but the boxes do not exist until 24 October. Re-cut the arc to the real dates.
Found a hole in the box plan: nobody has said who puts the striker strip on the printed sleeve. Raising it as a decision before the printer quotes.
Confirmed the e-way bill line is 50,000 rupees and that a live 'claimed' counter on the site must show real numbers - fake scarcity is a listed dark pattern
Re-read my own legal checklist, label rules and trademark notes before building the Drop 01 law map
Started the three design agendas - reading box concepts and the Instagram plan I already wrote so I build on them, not replace them.
Legal Team and Design Team renamed. Website Builder is on hold.
Got your match quality spec - veneer tray, poplar splints, one-strike damp-proof.
All 6 desks reported. 4 decisions really matter now, the rest can wait.
Tested all four drop states in a real browser: 75 checks, none failed, no errors and no sideways scrolling on phone or laptop.
Rewrote the founder guide: a new Part 3 covers opening a drop, closing it, updating the claimed count and reusing the site for Drop 02.
All four things are done. Buy 1,000 plain trays and 500 printed outers for about 12,500 rupees total. Your boxes would be in hand around 24 October.
One thing needs you: the price of the 3-box set. I recommend 279.
Redid all the numbers after Finance cut Drop 01 to 300 boxes - the pre-order gate is still 60 paid, which is now a fifth of the whole drop.
Four files delivered: the daily sales pipeline, the customer WhatsApp messages, the press and creator plan, and the drop calendar.
Sample plan done - order 50 boxes each from 3 vendors, about 1,500 rupees, with a 30-point scoring sheet. Writing the calendar now.
The site now has an always-open waitlist and a drop pre-order that opens and closes on dates you set.
Your vendor sheet is updated: EXAMPLE row gone, real contacts in, vendors ranked 1 to 8, seven Pune printers added and a new Stock tab.
New numbers: sell at 99, Drop 01 is 300 boxes, you get your money back at box 204, and Drop 02 only needs 73.
Trays are a one-off buy and printed outers repeat every drop, so Drop 02 breaks even at 73 boxes instead of 204.
A box now costs about 18 rupees landed instead of 9, so 79 rupees stops working and I am recommending 99.
Found working numbers for Asia Match, Bhish, Tritaon and Geewin, plus seven real Pune printers. Writing it all into your sheet now.
Customer messages written - the big one is never giving a non-Pune buyer a delivery date.
Sales pipeline page is done - it starts at zero on every line, which is honest.
Vendor contacts are mostly found. Now searching for Pune printers who will print small batches of outer boxes.
Checked the numbers in the Drop 01 plan, cafe pitch and finance files so the pipeline matches them.
Founder switched to reusable trays plus printed outer boxes, so I am rebuilding every number from scratch.
Started rebuilding the site so it has both an always-open waitlist and a drop pre-order with a live claimed counter.
Found real contact details for Asia Match, Bhish Exports, Tritaon and Epoch so far - company sites are blocked here so I am using search listings.
Starting on the daily sales pipeline, customer messages, press outreach and drop calendar.
Opened your vendor spreadsheet to see exactly what is already in it before I add anything.
Got your vendor sheet - 8 Sivakasi vendors, a call script and a Pune printers tab.
Team changed: Launch is now Sales and PR, and a new Production and Ops desk joined.
Website and guide are done - drag the website folder to netlify.com/drop and it is live in 4 minutes for zero rupees
Wrote the step-by-step guide for putting the site online free and switching on payments later
Launch and Sales finished. Couriers refuse matchboxes - Pune hand-delivery is the only way for now.
Checked colours for readability and made the page tiny (17 KB) so it loads instantly on phone data
Finance finished. 99 rupees is the price that works. 49 rupees loses money on delivery.
Correction to my earlier note: break-even is 150 boxes, not 140 - Legal confirmed a small registration cost I had not counted.
Checked my numbers against the finance agent's - a rider drop in Pune costs about 50 rupees, so hand-delivery and the 3-box set matter more than I first wrote. Both documents updated.
Three files are ready: what you keep per box, the break-even number, and a money tracker you can keep updating.
Raised a decision: the budget had no line at all for mailers and delivery, and that is the biggest cost per box. I have parked 3,000 there for now.
Legal finished. Real cost to start selling legally: about 500 rupees, not 3000.
Raised two things for you to decide - how we ship outside Pune, and building a 249 three-box set before any ads run.
The rule to remember: do not pay the 8,000 for boxes until 60 are pre-paid, and do not touch the 3,000 ad money until 150 boxes are sold.
All four documents are ready: the 500-box plan, the cafe pitch, the marketplace roadmap and the ads plan.
Legal work is finished. Total realistic cost to start selling legally in Pune: 500 rupees.
Checked the 10 brand names for obvious trademark trouble - drop Burn Book (Mean Girls / Paramount) and Phuljhadi (existing brand plus it means a firework).
Brand and Content finished - 10 names checked, 4 were already taken, 3 survive.
All three legal files are ready. The one thing to do this week: free Udyam registration at udyamregistration.gov.in - it takes 15 minutes and halves your future trademark fee.
Brand work done: 10 names with availability checked, 6 box designs, 30 days of Instagram, and a Pune seeding plan. I need you to pick the name before anything goes to print.
Synced my box back-panel with what Legal found - the words Safety Matches also have to go on the FRONT of every box.
Raised a decision you must answer before printing: whose postal address goes on the back of every box, because the law requires a real one.
The number that matters: you need to sell about 140 boxes to get your launch money back. If all 500 sell, the whole twenty thousand comes back and then some.
Cut the legal budget from 3,000 to 1,000 - almost everything you need in week 1 is free, which frees about 2,000 rupees for boxes.
Seeding plan done - 60 boxes out of the first 500, scripts for cafes and chai corners, and a tracking sheet.
Answer on price: sell at 99 rupees. At 49 rupees a delivered box loses you 21 rupees, because the rider alone costs 50.
Verified the real numbers: matches are taxed at 5 percent, Amazon charges no commission under 1,000 rupees, and a Pune rider drop costs about 45 rupees. Now doing the maths.
Label rules done - there is a ready-to-use box template your designer can work from, and the legal text must be at least 1mm tall.
Thirty days of Instagram is written - captions ready to paste, and a hard no-tobacco rule at the top so we do not get into trouble.
The website works: form validates, saves a backup copy, and shows a thank-you and share prompt
Cafe pitch written. Push the 60-rupee wholesale deal, 20 boxes, 1200 rupees cash.
Legal checklist is done - the whole week-1 list is free, and the only real licence is a 500 rupee Legal Metrology packer registration.
Supplier Scout is done. Big finding: 500 custom boxes is below what Sivakasi factories will make.
Drop 01 plan done. Now writing exactly what to say when you walk into a Pune cafe.
Six box designs written with exact hex codes and free Canva fonts. I say print three: Kaadepeti Classic, Pinkhead, Loadshedding.

All three files are ready, and I have raised one decision for you: 500 boxes is below what most factories will accept, so you need to choose between a sticker-sleeve test run or saving up for 5000 custom boxes.

Big one: matchboxes count as flammable goods, so normal couriers and India Post officially refuse them - that changes the whole delivery cost picture and I am pricing local Pune hand-delivery instead.
Important: matchboxes are not taxed at 18 percent. All matches were put on one low rate in 2021 and the low slab moved lower again in the Sept 2025 GST overhaul - I am nailing the exact figure.
Good news: a reseller of ordinary safety matches does not need an explosives licence - that is the factory's problem, not yours.
Raised decision D-002 - you choose the name. My pick is Kaadepeti. Now writing 6 box designs you can build in Canva tonight.
Bad news found early: matchboxes are on courier prohibited lists in India, so normal parcel delivery outside Pune is mostly blocked. Writing the plan around that.
Dashboard published as a private web link - you can open it on your phone.
Shortlist of 10 Sivakasi makers is written, with a source link for every contact detail.
Confirmed: matches sit in trademark Class 34, and a brand owner who gets boxes packed by a factory still has label duties.
Good news for Amazon later: Amazon India now charges zero commission on items under 1,000 rupees, only a small fixed fee - I am checking the exact 2026 numbers.
Ten names done. Four of them are already taken by real brands - good news, I found that out before you printed 500 boxes.
Have enough names and numbers - now writing the three files for you.
Checking whether matchboxes count as dangerous goods - this decides if Amazon, Flipkart and quick-commerce are even possible.
Found that selling online can force GST registration even below the 40 lakh limit - checking the exact rule now.
Got phone numbers for several Sivakasi match factories, including one called Sri Ramesh Colour Match Works.
Starting the money model - checking the real GST rate on matchboxes before I do any maths, because it is unusually low.
Heads up: I cannot open WHOIS or Instagram directly from here, so every availability call is search-evidence only and I say so in the file - you must confirm on a registrar before printing anything.
Started work on the 500-box sell-through plan, cafe pitch and marketplace roadmap.
Found a Sivakasi maker already selling matches with black heads - good sign for our look.
Started on brand names - 10 options coming, and I am actually checking domains before I claim anything is free.
Starting on the pre-order website - first checking which free form tools work without a backend
Found a big warning early: most Sivakasi factories only take orders of 50,000 boxes and up, not 500.
Checking whether someone who only SELLS safety matches needs an explosives licence, or only the factory that makes them.
Company websites are blocked on this machine, so I am gathering everything from search results and marking clearly what still needs a phone call.
Starting work on the legal checklist, packaging label rules, and trademark notes.
Started hunting for real matchstick makers in Sivakasi.
Shared state helper installed - all 6 agents can now report progress safely.
Matchbox HQ dashboard is built and running.
Budget loaded: 20,000 rupees total. Nothing spent yet.
All 6 team members briefed and started.
First decision is waiting for you: how we take money on day one.
